text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: The Puente Brillante Scholarship Fund, operating in the highland municipalities of San Ilario and Cerro Verde, awarded 412 scholarships to girls entering lower secondary school between January 2022 and June 2023. Retention among scholars reached 91 percent, compared with roughly sixty percent among non-scholar classmates in the same schools. Mentors met each scholar at least twice a month, and mothers attended three community sessions per term on average. However, the evaluation team found that transport stipends did not keep pace with rising bus fares, and eleven girls reported walking more than two hours each way. The programme has not yet established a tracking system for scholars who transfer to urban schools. Evaluators recommend revising the stipend formula before the 2024 school year begins.

passages.source_passage: At the midpoint of the Kalundi Clean Water Initiative, run by AquaVia Partners in Mbeleni District, 23 of the planned 40 boreholes had been drilled and commissioned. Water committees in fourteen villages now collect a monthly user fee of 500 shillings per household. Household latrine coverage rose from 38 percent at baseline in 2021 to 64 percent by March 2023. Hygiene promoters visited schools weekly, and pupils demonstrated handwashing at every observed session. Nonetheless, the evaluators noted that five boreholes were not functional at the time of the field visit, mostly because spare parts were not stocked locally. No village had yet budgeted for major repairs. The team recommends that the remaining drilling be paired with a district spare-parts depot.

passages.source_passage: Board members will recall that the Harvest Bridge cash transfer pilot in the Sorrel Valley began disbursing payments in October 2022. Since then, 2,150 households have received monthly transfers of 45 dollars through mobile wallets. Post-distribution monitoring shows that 78 percent of recipients spent most of the transfer on staple foods, while about one in five prioritised school fees. Market prices did not rise noticeably in the three main trading towns, which eases earlier concerns about inflation. However, enrolment has not reached the 3,000 households approved in the budget, because registration teams could not access two flooded sub-counties until April. Management asks the Board to approve a four-month no-cost extension so that the remaining households can be enrolled.

passages.source_passage: The Greenfurrow Farmer Field School network, coordinated by the Tamsin Rural Trust across Oberu and Lakashi provinces, has trained 1,860 smallholders in 74 schools since its launch in 2021. Participating farmers adopted an average of four of the six promoted practices, including mulching and intercropping with legumes. Maize yields among participants were 32 percent higher than among comparison farmers in the 2022 season. Female participation reached 58 percent, exceeding the target. The evaluation did not find evidence that farmers outside the schools were copying the practices, which weakens the programme's assumption of spontaneous spread. Facilitators also reported that seed fairs were never held in Lakashi because of procurement delays. The evaluators suggest assigning lead farmers to host open demonstration days for neighbours.

passages.source_passage: Shelterline International's case management service in the Darrow Plains camp opened 1,204 protection cases between July 2022 and December 2023, of which 41 percent involved unaccompanied or separated children. Caseworkers closed 690 cases after confirming that safety plans had been met. Average time from referral to first home visit fell from nine days to four. Refugees interviewed generally described caseworkers as respectful, and no complaints of breached confidentiality were recorded. However, the evaluation found that the service did not have enough Arabic-speaking female staff, so some women waited weeks for an appropriate caseworker. Referral pathways to the camp health clinic worked well, but links with the legal desk were weak. The evaluators recommend recruiting at least six additional female caseworkers before the next funding phase.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the second term of the 2023 school year for the Assiba Hot Meals Programme in the Konnaré and Fadéla districts. Partner schools served 186,400 hot lunches to an average of 3,240 pupils per day, and meals were provided on 54 of 58 scheduled school days. Cooks used locally purchased millet and cowpeas for roughly two-thirds of all meals. Attendance in partner schools averaged 88 percent, against 79 percent in non-partner schools nearby. Stock checks found that four schools did not maintain storeroom records, and one school had no functioning scale. Deliveries were delayed twice because the district road was not passable after heavy rain. Monitors observed that pupils washed their hands before eating at most visits.

passages.source_passage: The Quietharbour Community Counselling Service, run by the Mendel Wellbeing Collective in the coastal town of Port Aveline, delivered 2,736 individual sessions and 148 group sessions between March 2022 and August 2023. Lay counsellors, trained over twelve weeks, carried most of the caseload under fortnightly clinical supervision. Among clients completing at least six sessions, 67 percent showed a clinically meaningful drop in distress scores. Men made up only a quarter of clients, and outreach to fishing crews has not produced many referrals. The evaluators found no evidence of harm, but they noted that waiting lists were not reviewed systematically. Counsellors said supervision helped them manage difficult cases. The evaluation recommends piloting evening sessions at the harbour cooperative to reach working men.

passages.source_passage: Halfway through the Dryline Resilience Project, implemented by Terraverde Alliance in the semi-arid Ushenda Basin, 5,400 farming households had received drought-tolerant sorghum and pearl millet seed. Despite rainfall 30 percent below the long-term average in 2023, adopting households harvested enough grain to cover about seven months of consumption, compared with four months for non-adopters. Community seed banks were established in 19 of 25 target villages. The evaluators did not observe any decline in local seed diversity, which had been a concern at design stage. However, the planned weather information service wasn't launched, since the radio partner withdrew in late 2022. Extension officers trained farmers in zai pits and stone bunds. The team advises replacing the radio component with SMS-based advisories.

passages.source_passage: In its third year, the Kopa Pamoja Savings Programme, implemented by Riverstone Community Finance in the Ndalasi and Mpemba wards, supported 312 village savings and loan groups with 7,850 active members, 81 percent of them women. Cumulative savings reached the equivalent of 412,000 dollars during the 2023 reporting year, and the average loan size was 38 dollars. Repayment rates stayed above 95 percent in all wards. No group reported losing funds to theft, which members credited to the three-key lockbox system. Graduation of groups to independent status was slower than planned, and 46 groups did not complete their share-out on schedule. Field officers also noted that young men were rarely joining. We propose using the remaining grant period to train community-based trainers who can support groups without staff visits.

passages.source_passage: This update summarises the first eighteen months of the Justice Within Reach paralegal service operated by the Calder Legal Empowerment Network in the Vessaro and Thornmere counties. Our 36 community paralegals have handled 2,980 cases, most commonly land disputes, inheritance claims and unpaid wages. Around 62 percent of cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Paralegals referred 214 cases to partner lawyers, and the bar association provided pro bono representation in most of them. We have not met the target for women clients, who account for 44 percent against a goal of 50 percent. Several paralegals in Thornmere haven't received their bicycle allowances since September 2023, which has limited visits to remote villages. Management requests Board approval to reallocate savings from the training budget to cover these allowances.
